empty.printersBody: Printers here are added by hand. To sync them from an account, allow printers on it in Integrations.
empty.printsBody: Prints here are added by hand. To sync them from an account, allow prints on it in Integrations.
empty.spoolsBody: Spools here are added by hand. To sync them from an account, allow spools on it in Integrations.
empty.catalogBody: Brands, models and materials here are added by hand; presets come from a slicer, an account or a zip. Add a slicer or an account in Integrations, or pick a machine as the hub's slicer.

catalog.fromDevice: The machine's connector sends this slicer's system presets whenever a slicer update changes them. Until it has, the catalog stays as it is.
catalog.receiveOn: Receive the system presets, brands and printer models in {{slicer}} on {{machine}}
catalog.noCopy: The hub has no catalog yet
catalog.mismatch: Not sent: slicer {{here}} here, catalog from {{source}}
catalog.waiting: Waiting for the slicer to close

presets.notReported: {{slicer}} is no longer found on this machine.
presets.noReport: Waiting for the machine's first report
presets.outdated: That machine's connector is too old for this. Update it from Hub management, then try again.
presets.waiting_one: {{count}} waiting for the slicer to close
presets.waiting_other: {{count}} waiting for the slicer to close

picks.none: No picks yet: it receives nothing from the server.
picks.exists: This machine has this pick already.
picks.hint: {{machine}} works as {{user}}. Edit sends the machine's saves back to the server; Read keeps the files read-only there. It never gets more than {{user}} may see or edit, and if the machine's user changes, the new user's rights apply.
picks.removeConfirm: Its files leave {{machine}}, except ones changed there that the server doesn't have yet. Nothing on the server changes.

folders.empty: Machines that share folders with the server or receive projects from it are listed here. Turn on Share to server or Receive from server on a machine's page in Hub management.
folders.notReported: Its connector hasn't sent its shared folders yet. Update the connector, then they show here.
folders.addConfirm: Its projects become visible to the people who can see {{machine}}'s projects.
folders.covered: This folder is shared already, inside another shared folder.
folders.removeConfirm: Project folders inside it stay, shown as not shared, until it's shared again. Nothing on the machine changes.

loadError: Couldn't load settings. Is the server running?

general.tagsHint: Off hides tags everywhere. Your tags are kept, and turning this back on restores them.
general.accountsHint: Off: nobody signs in and the app works for a single user, as before accounts existed. Users and roles are kept, and turning this back on restores them; then everyone signs in again.
general.accountsHubOn: Turn the hub off first: it needs user accounts.
general.accountsOffBody: Nobody needs to sign in any more, and everyone who reaches the app has full access. Users and roles are kept for when you turn accounts back on.
general.accountsOffLocal: This server has no APP_PASSWORD, so only this PC will reach the app.

branding.title: Branding
branding.everyone: Applies to everyone who uses this server.
branding.name: App name
branding.nameHint: Shown in the sidebar and browser tab. Leave empty for the default.
branding.error: Couldn't update the image. Use a PNG, JPEG or WebP up to 5 MB.

logo.label: Logo
logo.hint: Replaces the icon in the sidebar.

favicon.label: Favicon
favicon.hint: The small icon in the browser tab.

costs.lifetimeHint: Purchase price is spread over this many hours as printer wear. 0 leaves wear out of costs. Each printer can override it.
costs.maintenanceHint: Spreads what you logged on maintenance tasks over the printer's runtime. Each printer can override it.
costs.printerCountHint: Off leaves printer wear and maintenance out of costs. Each printer can override it; accessories follow their own setting.
costs.accessoryCountHint: Prints made while an accessory was on the printer pay its wear and maintenance too.
costs.accessoryLifetimeHint: Purchase price is spread over this many hours as accessory wear. 0 leaves it out.
costs.accessoryMaintenanceHint: Spreads what you logged on an accessory's maintenance tasks over its runtime.

projects.rootInUse: Projects still use this folder, maybe archived ones. Unlink or delete them first, then remove it.
projects.rootExists: This folder is a project folder already.
projects.rootMissing: That folder doesn't exist on the server.
projects.rootMissingDevice: That folder doesn't exist on the device.
projects.rootNested: This folder is inside another project folder on that device, or holds one.
projects.rootNotShared: The machine doesn't share this folder. Share it first in Projects settings → Sources.
projects.deviceOffline: The device is offline. Start its connector, then try again.
projects.deviceTimeout: The device didn't answer. Check that its connector is running, then try again.
projects.editByDevice: The device's own user can always edit.
projects.maxFilesHint: The most files a scan lists per project folder. Files past the limit can't be picked as preview, description or gallery image. A higher limit slows scans and makes the project list heavier, so raise it only for folders that really hold more files.
projects.deviceFolderMaxHint: How much one folder's scan on a device may send to the hub: descriptions, cover, plate previews and gallery picks, in that order. Whatever doesn't fit is left out, so plate previews are dropped first. Up to {{max}} MB; a change sends the folders again.
projects.viewerMaxHint: Larger model files show the plate thumbnail instead of loading in the 3D viewer.
projects.uploadMaxHint: Largest file that can be uploaded into a project folder.
projects.trashHint: Files deleted in the app go to a hidden trash folder in their project folder until you empty it.
projects.trashConfirm: The deleted files are removed for good. This can't be undone.
projects.trashError: Couldn't empty the trash. A file in it may be in use.

relink.title: Change project folder
relink.hint: Projects keep their subfolder. If you already moved the files, leave Move files off: only the app's link changes, nothing on disk.
relink.moveFiles: Move files from the previous folder to the new one
relink.confirm_one: Change the project folder of {{count}} project to {{path}}? A project whose subfolder isn't there will show as missing.
relink.confirm_other: Change the project folder of {{count}} projects to {{path}}? Projects whose subfolder isn't there will show as missing.
relink.confirmMove_one: Change the project folder of {{count}} project to {{path}} and move its files there?
relink.confirmMove_other: Change the project folder of {{count}} projects to {{path}} and move their files there?
relink.error: Couldn't change the project folder. You may not be allowed to edit that folder.
relink.unlinkBody: Nothing on disk changes, and each project keeps everything it knows. Scans leave the folders alone, so they don't come back as new projects. Link a folder again on its project's edit page. A folder that is missing is just forgotten.

skips.same_root: It's already in that project folder.
skips.folder_in_use: Another project already uses that folder. It may be archived.
skips.scan_failed: Its folder couldn't be read, so nothing changed.
skips.move_unavailable: Files on a device can't be moved from here. Move them yourself, then change the project folder with Move files off.
skips.folder_exists: A file with the same name is already in the new folder, so nothing moved.
skips.invalid_folder: The new folder is inside the current one, so nothing moved.
skips.move_failed: Moving the files failed. Some may already be in the new folder, so check both.
skips.failed: It couldn't be changed. Try again.

projects.autoSliceHint: Auto slice: when a sliced 3MF in one of the folder's projects changes, its plates are sliced again with their saved setup. Each project can change this in its print setup.
projects.removeConfirm: {{path}} stops being watched. Its files stay where they are.

folder.notFound: This project folder doesn't exist any more.
folder.sourceHint: Where the folder is: on this server, or in a folder a machine shares.
folder.pathHub: The folder's full path on this server.
folder.pathDevice: A folder in the machine's shared folders. It stays on that machine: its connector watches it and sends the projects to the server.
folder.pathFixed: The path can't change. To use another folder, add it as a new project folder.
folder.layoutGroups_other: Projects inside {{count}} levels of group folders
folder.layoutHint: A folder that holds a model file is a project even higher up, and its subfolders aren't searched for more projects.
folder.filesNone: Only files in the project folder
folder.filesHint: Which files of a project are listed and watched for changes. Fewer levels keep a big unpacked download cheap.
folder.depthChangedHub: Projects already found stay as they are. The next scan (Scan folders on Projects) adds the projects it finds at the new level; none are moved or merged.
folder.depthChangedDevice: The machine lists the folder again when you save: projects no longer at a project level show as missing, and the ones at the new level are added.
folder.filesChangedHub: Each project's file list changes at the next scan.
folder.filesChangedDevice: The machine sends the projects' file lists again when you save.
folder.rescanHint: Catches changes the folder watcher misses, on network shares (SMB, NFS) and cloud folders. Only folders that changed are read again. Not needed on a local disk.
folder.rescanAtHint: In the server's time zone, for a folder on a machine too. Any time: counted from the last rescan.

editBy.roles: All users who can edit projects

folder.editByHub: Everyone else who sees the projects can still view and download the files.
folder.editByDevice: {{user}}, this machine's user, can always edit.

example.title: Example
example.hint: How this folder is read with the settings on this page.
example.layoutFlat: Every folder right inside {{folder}} is a project.
example.filesAll: All of a project's files are listed.
example.filesNone: Only the files right in a project folder are listed.
example.filesLevels_one: Files up to {{count}} subfolder level down are listed.
example.filesLevels_other: Files up to {{count}} subfolder levels down are listed.

alerts.hint: Alerts appear in the Alerts page. Optionally also send them to a phone or inbox.
alerts.uncovered_one: No enabled user gets the {{kinds}} alert.
alerts.uncovered_other: No enabled user gets these alerts: {{kinds}}.
alerts.maintenanceLeadHours: Maintenance warning (print hours before due, 0 = none)

prints.paceHint: Estimates a duration for imported prints that have grams but no time: your own prints' pace when there are enough of them, else this.
prints.label: Failure reasons
prints.hint: One per line. Offered when a print fails or is cancelled.

printers.defaultHint: Used for the cost estimate on a project page (its wear, maintenance and energy figures). Pick another printer there any time. Without one, the first printer is used.
printers.label: Printer states
printers.hint: One per line. The first is used for new printers. Known names (working, maintenance, inop, retired) are translated.

orders.label: Order statuses
orders.hint: One per line, in the order an order moves through them. The first is used for new orders. Known names (accepted, in_progress, done, canceled) are translated.

backup.hint: A backup holds your database, photos and the key that protects saved logins, so keep the file private. Restoring replaces all current data.
backup.keepHint: Older automatic backups are deleted. Backups you create yourself are never removed.
backup.error: That didn't work. Check that the file is a backup made by this app.
backup.restaged: Backup ready. Restart the app to finish restoring; your current data is kept in the pre-restore folder.
backup.confirmBody: All current data is replaced by the backup when you restart the app.

server.current: In use: {{value}} ({{source}}). Leave empty to use the default.
server.restart: Restart required: the saved values apply the next time the app starts. A flag or environment variable still overrides them.
server.passwordNeeded: Reaching the app from other devices needs the APP_PASSWORD environment variable. Without it, only requests addressed to localhost or this host are accepted.
server.startAtLoginHint: Starts the app when you sign in to this computer. Turn it off to remove the entry.
server.stopBody: The app stops and every open tab loses connection. Start it again from the desktop or Start-menu shortcut.
server.networkHint: Changes to the host or port apply only after a restart (or after you stop the server and start it again).

public.title: Public address
public.autoHint: Links in alerts use the host and port above, or this computer's first network address.
public.internalHint: An address of this computer on your network, for links opened from your home or office.
public.externalHint: The address you reach the app at from outside, such as behind a reverse proxy. Include http:// or https://.
public.invalid: Enter an address that starts with http:// or https://.
public.link: Alerts link to {{value}}. Applies at once, no restart.
public.noLink: Alerts carry no link. Choose an address above to add one.
public.fixed: Set by the APP_PUBLIC_URL environment variable: {{value}}
public.mayBeFalse: The test runs from the server, and a home router often can't reach its own external address from inside, so this can be a false alarm. You can still save it. Use Open address to check from this device.

result.notFound: The name wasn't found. Check the spelling and your DNS.
result.refused: Nothing answered at this address and port.
result.certificate: The HTTPS certificate isn't valid for this address.
result.otherServer: Something answered, but it isn't this server (or it redirected).
result.hostNotAllowed: This server refused the name. Add it to APP_ALLOWED_HOSTS.

hub.enabledHint: Lets workstations, a NAS or a file server join this server with a small connector app, so project folders on those devices show up here and folders on this server can sync to them. Off: nothing changes.
hub.needsUsers: The hub needs user accounts, because each device acts as a user. Add an admin account under Users first.
hub.needsAccountsOn: The hub needs user accounts, because each device acts as a user. Turn on user accounts under General first.

logs.hint: Keeps a record of what the app does in its database, for troubleshooting. Credentials are never written.
logs.daysHint: Older entries are removed every hour.
logs.maxHint: The oldest entries beyond this are removed every hour.

updates.channelHint: Stable gets releases only. Dev also gets pre-releases, for testers.
updates.checkFailed: Could not reach GitHub to check for updates.
updates.manualGit: This install can’t update itself. In the app’s folder, stop the app and run:
updates.manualDocker: Docker installs update by pulling the new image. Next to your docker-compose.yml, run:
updates.wentBack: Updating to {{version}} failed while {{step}}. You are still on {{current}}; the Logs and the terminal say more.

steps.node: checking Node.js: it needs Node.js {{node}} or newer

updates.confirmUpdateBody: A backup is made first. The app then restarts, and is away for about a minute while it installs. If anything fails, it goes back to this version.
updates.confirmRollBackBody: The app goes back to that version and restores the backup made before the update. Everything changed since {{date}} is lost.

errors.dirty: The app’s folder has local changes, so it can’t switch versions. Undo them (git status shows them) and try again.
errors.fetch_failed: Could not download the update. Check the internet connection.
errors.git_failed: git did not run. Is it installed?
errors.invalid_backup: The backup for this version can’t be read.
errors.bad_checksum: The download was damaged (its checksum doesn’t match), so it wasn’t installed. Try again later.
errors.needs_installer: This version needs a newer Node.js than the installed app has. Download its installer from the release page (What’s new) and run it; your data stays.
